note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent auditor, after 4bf9935e38 and 29419d46cf). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 7.6.5: "Otherwise, if this ancestor is a case node, the leaf MUST exist if any node from the case exists in the data tree." The row's {gap} is gone and the code now does it. walkTree resolves each data key through schemaChild, which descends through choice and case entries, so case data is type-checked and walked; requireMandatoryChildren handles a choice child by requireMandatoryInPresentCases, which runs requireMandatoryChildren over every case for which holdsData finds a node in the map holding the choice, and skips the rest. Shapes checked by probe (go test -overlay, nothing written to the tree): a mandatory leaf directly in a case; below non-presence containers a present case holds (walked through schemaChild, then requireMandatoryUnderAbsent); a non-presence container ABSENT inside a case that has another node present is still required (closest qualifying ancestor is the case); a presence container inside a case owes its leaf only when present; a case inside a nested choice (inner choice handled by the IsChoice branch of requireMandatoryChildren on the outer case); an implicit case: goyang's FixChoice wraps each shorthand node in a CaseEntry, so a shorthand container's mandatory leaf is checked against the container's own map and reported as wrap/shc/m, with no false error when supplied. goyang refuses a choice as shorthand of a choice, so that shape cannot be loaded. Negative TestRFC7950MandatoryRequiredWhenCaseExists asserts the exact missing path, the set command and that it is the only missing path for each of the three placements; positive TestRFC7950MandatoryNotRequiredForAbsentCase asserts zero errors with no case present and with each case complete. The .ci drives ze config validate over a gre tunnel with local ip and no remote ip and requires exit 1, the path interface/tunnel[gre0]/encapsulation/gre/remote/ip and the set command. Question 2 judged by my own mutants, not by the records: (A) requireMandatoryInPresentCases checks every case regardless of holdsData: positive goes red in all four subtests and the negative too; (B) it checks no case: negative goes red (leaf in case, leaf in nested case); (C) walkTree reverted to the pre-fix entry.Dir lookup: negative goes red (leaf below containers, empty container), and ze config validate over the .ci's config prints 'configuration valid' and exits 0, so the .ci discriminates the defect it names. The recorded revert breaks (panic in requireMandatoryInPresentCases; panic in schemaChild, which crashes ze at schema load) prove only that the units reach those producers; they are coarse, but they do not weaken this verdict because the mutants above show both polarities fail on the actual non-compliance in each direction. The .ci record is worth re-recording on the mutant route (for example the entry.Dir lookup in walkTree), since a crash at schema load turns every .ci red. Population: the case-scoped mandatory leaves in shipped modules are iface tunnel remote/ip (tunnel-v4/v6-endpoints) and vxlan vni; static and bfd hold mandatory choices (Section 7.9.4, not this row). One reading to note: an empty non-presence container written in a case (gre { }) counts as the case existing, which is the strict reading and fails closed. All tagged units green at HEAD; ./le rfc discriminate id RFC7950-7.6.5-2 lists three records, none stale or unproven.
